newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels take Mobutu birthplace-Western sources.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels take Mobutu birthplace-Western sources.

text.p: Zairean rebels have captured the birthplace of President Mobutu Sese Seko at Lisala and are moving toward his huge jungle palace at Gbadolite, Western security sources said on Saturday.
"Lisala has fallen. The rebels are now heading towards Gemena and Gbadolite on foot, by boat and by road," the sources told Reuters in the Zaire capital.

The sources said Lisala, a town on the Zaire river, had been captured by the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire in the past two days. The sources did not give details of the fighting.
Gbadolite, where Mobutu has spent much of his time in recent years, is 300 km (190 miles) north of Lisala on a road which is good by Zairean standards.
Diplomats in the Angolan capital on Saturday said rebel leader Laurent Kabila was apparently on his way to join a peace summit with Mobutu on a South African ship.
Since launching their rebellion seven months ago Kabila's rebels have captured over three quarters of the vast central African state, including all major towns outside Kinshasa.
